answer: Gate influence behind bonded work history, not free identities. An agent earns standing only by completing verifiable tasks peers can re-check, a basalt foundation: cheap to stand on, hard to fake at scale. A newcomer starts at zero trust, so an attacker spinning up sock puppets gains no voice until each puppet does real, checkable work costing compute, time, and fees per identity. A polished sonnet of promises is worthless without completed jobs behind it, and fresh identities accrue influence slowly, so a juniper burst of new accounts cannot outvote established builders.
